name: London Ambulance Service
description:
The London Ambulance Service dispatches ambulances in emergencies. 
    The key goal is to allocate an available ambulance for every call that can reach the scene within 11 minutes. 
    The entire dispatch process must not exceed a set maximum time limit.

    To make this work, the computer system (CAD) analyzes incident forms and assigns vehicles. 
    It is vital to track the exact location of moving ambulances. 
    This requires staff to follow standard routes and correctly communicate departure and destination, 
    allowing radio operators and the CAD to record data accurately.

The London Ambulance Service dispatches ambulances in emergencies. 
    The key goal is to allocate an available ambulance for every call that can reach the scene within 11 minutes. 
    The entire dispatch process must not exceed a set maximum time limit.

    To make this work, the computer system (CAD) analyzes incident forms and assigns vehicles. 
    It is vital to track the exact location of moving ambulances. 
    This requires staff to follow standard routes and correctly communicate departure and destination, 
    allowing radio operators and the CAD to record data accurately.
highLevelGoals: Allocate an available ambulance for every emergency call that can reach the scene within 11 minutes, ensuring rapid response to emergencies.
Utilize the computer-aided dispatch system to analyze incident forms and automatically assign vehicles to emergency calls, enhancing efficiency in the dispatch process.
Track the exact location of moving ambulances to ensure efficient routing and timely arrival at emergency scenes.
Ensure clear and accurate communication between ambulance drivers and dispatch operators to coordinate operations effectively.
Process emergency calls efficiently to initiate the dispatch process without delays, ensuring a quick response to emergencies.
Ensure that the entire dispatch process does not exceed a set maximum time limit to maintain efficiency and compliance with operational standards.
lowLevelGoals: Receive an emergency call from the public and log the details into the system.
Record the details of the incident including location, type of emergency, and caller information into the system.
Analyze the logged incident details to determine the appropriate response and available resources.
Query the system for available ambulances that can respond to the incident based on location and availability.
Automatically assign the identified available ambulance to the incident based on the analysis.
Send a dispatch notification to the assigned ambulance with incident details and location.
Continuously monitor and update the location of the dispatched ambulance in real-time.
Update the dispatch status in the system as the ambulance progresses towards the incident location.
Send and receive messages between the dispatch operators and the ambulance drivers to coordinate operations.
Receive confirmation from the ambulance driver upon arrival at the incident scene.
Record the total time taken for the dispatch process to ensure compliance with operational standards.

baselineCritiques.highLevelGoals: Major omission and contradiction. The provided goals list includes 'Computer-Aided Dispatch System' as an actor for two goals. According to the GORE framework definition provided, actors are active entities (like humans or external systems) that perform actions, whereas the CAD is the system being built. Goals should be attributed to human stakeholders (e.g., Dispatch Operators, Management) who have the need for the system to perform these functions. Additionally, the goal 'Enforce Maximum Dispatch Process Time' is attributed to the system itself rather than the stakeholder who requires this constraint (e.g., Management or Dispatch Operators). The goals should reflect the stakeholders' needs (the 'why') rather than the system's internal functions (the 'how').
baselineCritiques.lowLevelGoals: The low-level goals provided are largely functional and align well with the high-level goals and system description. However, there is a significant omission regarding the specific constraint mentioned in the description
